'''Jerome Goddard''' (born 1957) is an American [[entomologist]] currently located at [[Mississippi State University]] who is known for research on a number of medically important [[arthropod]]s, most notably ticks<ref>{{cite journal|last=Goddard|first=J.|author2=Varela-Stokes, A.|journal=Vet. Parasitol.|year=2009|volume=160|issue=1–2|pages=1–12|pmid=19054615|doi=10.1016/j.vetpar.2008.10.089|title=Role of the lone star tick, Amblyomma americanum (L.), in human and animal diseases}}</ref>  and the common [[bed bug]].<ref>{{cite journal|last=Goddard|first=J.|author2=deShazo, R.D.|title=Bed bugs and clinical consequences of their bites|journal=J. Am. Med. Assoc.|year=2009|volume=301|issue=13|pages=1358–66|pmid=19336711|doi=10.1001/jama.2009.405|doi-access=free}}</ref> His work on the health effects of bed bugs has helped clarify the [[pathophysiology]] of cutaneous reactions to their bites.<ref>{{cite journal|last=Goddard|first=J. |author2=Hasenkampf, H. |author3=Edwards, K. |author4=de Shazo, R.D. |author5=Embers, M.E. |title=Bed bug saliva causes release of monocytic inflammatory mediators: plausible cause of cutaneous bite reactions|journal=Int. Arch. Allergy Immunol.|year=2013|volume=161|issue=2|pages=127–130|pmid=23343710|doi=10.1159/000345134}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|last=Goddard|first=J.|author2=Edwards, K.T.|title=Effects of bed bug saliva on human skin|journal=JAMA Dermatology|year=2013|volume=149|issue=3|pages=372–373|doi=10.1001/jamadermatol.2013.878}}</ref> 

Prior to coming to Mississippi State, Goddard was an Air Force medical entomologist for 3 years and then State Medical Entomologist for the Mississippi Department of Health for 20 years. After [[Hurricane Katrina]] (2005), Goddard was the health department official responsible for the mosquito and vector control program along the Mississippi Gulf Coast.<ref>{{cite journal|last=Spear|first=S.|title=After the Storm|journal=Environmental Health Practitioner (U.K.)|year=2007|issue=November 7, 2007}}</ref>  He is the author of a medical textbook used by physicians<ref>{{cite book|last=Goddard|first=Jerome|title=The Physician's Guide to Arthropods of Medical Importance, 6th Edition|year=2013|publisher=Taylor and Francis (CRC)|location=Boca Raton, Florida|isbn=9781439850855|pages=514}}</ref> which won "Highly Commended" in 2003 in the British Medical Association's Best Medical Book of the Year competition. Over the last two decades Goddard has served as an educational resource concerning medically important arthropods to a U.S. Congressional Committee,<ref>{{cite web|last=U.S. House Committee Testimony (1999) |title=The Impact of the Food Quality Protection Act Implementation on Public Health|url=http://commdocs.house.gov/committees/ag/hag10629.000/hag10629_0.htm}}</ref>  in various newspapers and magazines such as Reader's Digest,<ref>{{cite journal|last=Chen|first=I.|title=How to beat the bugs of summer|journal=Reader's Digest|year=2002|issue=July 2002|pages=144–149}}</ref> and on television programs such as The Learning Channel ("Living with Bugs")<ref>{{cite web|last=Fitch|first=Anna|title=Living with Bugs: Close Encounters|url=https://www.imdb.com/title/tt1173514/combined|publisher=The Learning Channel (Oxford Scientific Films)}}</ref> and the ''Colbert Report''.<ref>{{cite web |title=Episode 6117: Threatdown - Bedbugs & Environmentalists - Jerome Goddard |url=https://www.cc.com/video/5klha6/the-colbert-report-threatdown-bedbugs-environmentalists-jerome-goddard |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210123022842/https://www.cc.com/video/5klha6/the-colbert-report-threatdown-bedbugs-environmentalists-jerome-goddard |url-status=dead |archive-date=January 23, 2021 |website=Colbert Report |access-date=2023-11-15}}</ref>
